cues.zh: 大家好。这个视频是我前一段时间做的一场演讲的录像。我已经在第二个频道上发布过一版了，但你们知道我还有个第二频道吗？大多数人都不知道。我觉得应该有更多人看到它，所以我重新制作了。我做了清理，改进了画面，没错，就是这个。希望你们喜欢。好的。

cues.en: Hello everyone.
cues.zh: 大家好。

cues.en: My name is Robert Miles. I am usually doing this on YouTube. I'm not really used to public speaking.
cues.zh: 我叫Robert Miles。我通常在YouTube上做这些。我不太习惯当众演讲。

cues.en: I'm not used to
cues.zh: 我不习惯

cues.en: not being able to edit out my mistakes.
cues.zh: 没法把错误剪掉。

cues.zh: 可能会有错误，我也可能讲得太快。

cues.en: Sorry, not sorry. So when it comes to AI safety, you can kind of divide it up into four areas along two axes. You've got your short term and your long term and you've got
cues.zh: 抱歉，但也不抱歉。说到AI安全，你可以沿着两个轴把它分成四个领域。有短期和长期，还有

cues.en: accident risks and misuse risks and
cues.zh: 事故风险和滥用风险，

cues.en: that's kind of a useful way to divide things up. AI safety covers everything. The area that interests me most is the long term accident risks. I think once you have very powerful AI systems,
cues.zh: 这样划分挺有用的。AI安全涵盖一切。我最感兴趣的领域是长期事故风险。我认为一旦你有了非常强大的AI系统，

cues.en: it almost doesn't matter if they're being
cues.zh: 它们是被

cues.en: used by the right people or the wrong people or what you're trying to do with them. The difficulty is in keeping them in under control at all. So that's what I'm going to be talking about.
cues.zh: 对的人还是错的人使用，或者你想用它们做什么，几乎都不重要了。困难在于能不能把它们控制住。所以这就是我要讲的内容。

cues.en: What is AI safety? Why is it important?
cues.zh: 什么是AI安全？为什么它很重要？

cues.en: So I want to start by asking the question which I think everybody needs to be asking themselves.
cues.zh: 所以我想先问一个问题，我认为每个人都应该问问自己。

cues.en: What is the most important problem in your field?
cues.zh: 你的领域里最重要的问题是什么？

cues.en: Take a second to think of it
cues.zh: 花一秒钟想想

cues.en: And why are you not working on that?
cues.zh: 那你为什么不做这个？

cues.en: For me, I think the most important problem in the field of AI is AI safety.
cues.zh: 对我来说，我认为AI领域最重要的问题是AI安全。

cues.en: This is the problem specifically that I'm worried about, that we will sooner or later build an artificial agent with general intelligence.
cues.zh: 我具体担心的正是这个问题：我们迟早会构建出具有通用智能的人工智能体。

cues.en: So I'm going to go into a bunch of these terms.
cues.zh: 接下来我要讲几个术语。

cues.en: The first thing is what do I mean when I say sooner or later?
cues.zh: 第一个是，我说的“迟早”是什么意思？

cues.en: This is a little bit washed out, but this is a graph
cues.zh: 这个说法有点模糊，但这是一张图

cues.en: of a survey, a large survey of AI experts. These are people who published in major AI conferences
cues.zh: 来自一项调查，一项针对AI专家的大型调查。这些人都在主要AI会议上发表过论文

cues.en: and they were asked when they thought we would achieve
cues.zh: 他们被问到，认为我们何时能实现

cues.en: high level machine intelligence, which is defined as an agent which is able to carry out any task humans can as well as or better than humans.
cues.zh: 高水平机器智能，其定义是一个智能体能够完成人类能做的任何任务，且表现与人类相当或更好。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: they say that 50%
cues.zh: 他们说有50%

cues.en: chance of of
cues.zh: 的可能性

cues.en: having achieved that we hit that about forty five years from 2016,
cues.zh: 实现这一点，大约是从2016年起的四十五年，

cues.en: but then of course we hit like 10% chance nine years from now.
cues.zh: 但当然，从现在起九年也有10%的可能性。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: it's not immediate,
cues.zh: 这不是马上发生，

cues.en: but it's happening. This is definitely worth taking with a pinch of salt because if you ask the question slightly differently, you get an estimate of a hundred and twenty years rather than forty five.
cues.zh: 但它正在发生。这确实要打个折扣来看，因为如果你稍微换个问法，得到的估计是一百二十年而不是四十五年。

cues.en: There's a lot of uncertainty
cues.zh: 这个领域有很多不确定性

cues.en: in this area, but the point is it's going to happen as I said sooner or later because at the end of the day,
cues.zh: 但关键是，正如我所说，它迟早会发生，因为归根结底，

cues.en: general intelligence is possible,
cues.zh: 通用智能是可能的，

cues.en: the brain implements it and the brain is not magic.
cues.zh: 大脑实现了它，而大脑并非魔法。

cues.en: And sooner or later we'll figure it out.
cues.zh: 迟早我们会弄明白的。

cues.en: So what do I mean when I say an artificial agent?
cues.zh: 那么我说的“人工代理”是什么意思呢？

cues.en: Well, an agent is a term from
cues.zh: 代理这个词主要来自

cues.en: economics mostly,
cues.zh: 经济学，

cues.en: but basically agents have goals, they choose actions to further their goals. That is the simplest expression of what an agent is. So
cues.zh: 但基本上，代理有目标，它们选择行动以推进目标。这是对代理最简单的表述。所以

cues.en: the simplest thing that you might call an agent would be something like a thermostat. It has a goal which is to have the room be at a particular temperature. It has actions it can take. It can turn on the heating. It can turn on the air conditioning.
cues.zh: 你能称之为代理的最简单的东西，大概就是恒温器之类的东西。它有一个目标，就是让房间保持在特定温度。它有可以采取的行动。它可以打开暖气。它可以打开空调。

cues.en: It chooses its actions to achieve its goal of maintaining the room at a steady temperature. Extremely simple agent. A more complex agent might be something like a chess AI,
cues.zh: 它选择行动来实现将房间维持在稳定温度的目标。极其简单的代理。更复杂的代理可能是像国际象棋AI这样的东西，

cues.en: which has a goal of...
cues.zh: 它的目标是……

cues.en: Like if it's playing white, it has a goal of the black king being in checkmate. And it takes actions in the form of moving pieces on the board in order to achieve its goal. So you see how this idea of an agent is a very useful way of thinking about lots of different intelligent systems. And of course, humans can be modeled as agents as well. This is how it's usually done in economics.
cues.zh: 比如，如果它执白棋，它的目标是将黑方的王将死。它通过棋盘上移动棋子的形式采取行动来实现目标。所以你看到了，代理这个概念是思考许多不同智能系统的一种非常有用的方式。当然，人类也可以被建模为代理。这就是经济学中通常的做法。

cues.en: Individuals or companies
cues.zh: 个人或公司

cues.en: could be considered to have a goal of you know, maximizing their income or maximizing their profits and making decisions in order to achieve that.
cues.zh: 可以被认为有一个目标，你知道，就是最大化他们的收入或最大化他们的利润，并为此做出决策。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: when I'm talking about intelligence,
cues.zh: 当我在谈论智能时，

cues.en: intelligence has a lot of as a term is a heavily loaded term has a lot of different people put their own definitions on it. In this context what I mean when I say intelligence is just the thing that lets an agent choose effective actions.
cues.zh: 智能这个词承载了很多含义，很多人对它有自己的定义。在这个语境下，我说的智能就是让代理选择有效行动的东西。

cues.en: It's
cues.zh: It's

cues.en: whatever it is that's in our brains or that's in the programming of these systems that means that the actions they choose tend to get them closer to their goals.
cues.zh: 不管它是什么，存在于我们大脑中的，或者这些系统程序中的，意味着它们所选择的行动往往会让它们更接近目标。

cues.en: And so then you could say that
cues.zh: 于是你可以说

cues.en: an agent is more intelligent if it's more effective at achieving its goals, whatever those goals are. If you have two agents in an environment with incompatible goals,
cues.zh: 如果一个智能体更有效地实现其目标，无论那些目标是什么，它就更智能。如果你在一个环境中有两个目标不兼容的智能体，

cues.en: like let's say the environment is the chessboard and one agent wants white to win and one agent wants black to win, then
cues.zh: 比如环境是棋盘，一个智能体想让白方赢，一个想让黑方赢，那么

cues.en: generally the more intelligent agent will be the one that gets what it wants.
cues.zh: 通常更智能的智能体会是得偿所愿的那个。

cues.en: The better AI will win the chess game.
cues.zh: 更好的AI会赢得棋局。

cues.en: And finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: general intelligence. This is where it becomes
cues.zh: 通用智能。这就是我认为变得

cues.en: interesting in my opinion. So generality is the ability to behave intelligently in a wide range of domains. If you take something like a chess AI,
cues.zh: 有趣的地方。通用性是在广泛领域中表现出智能行为的能力。如果你拿一个国际象棋AI来说，

cues.en: it's extremely narrow. It only knows how to play chess.
cues.zh: 它极其狭窄。它只知道怎么下棋。

cues.en: And even though you might say that it's more intelligent than a thermostat because it's more sophisticated, it's more complicated,
cues.zh: 尽管你可能会说它比恒温器更智能，因为它更精密、更复杂，

cues.en: it couldn't do the thermostat's job.
cues.zh: 但它做不了恒温器的工作。

cues.en: There's no
cues.zh: 棋盘上没有任何

cues.en: position on the chessboard that corresponds to the room being a good temperature. There's no move that corresponds to turning on an air conditioner.
cues.zh: 位置对应于房间温度适宜。没有任何一步棋对应于打开空调。

cues.en: The chess AI can only think in terms of chess. It's extremely narrow.
cues.zh: 国际象棋AI只能以国际象棋的方式思考。它极其狭窄。

cues.en: Generality is a continuous spectrum.
cues.zh: 通用性是一个连续谱。

cues.en: So if you write a program that can play an Atari game, that's very narrow.
cues.zh: 所以如果你写一个能玩Atari游戏的程序，那是非常狭窄的。

cues.en: DeepMind, one of their early triumphs was that they made a program that could play dozens of different Atari games, single program that could learn all of these different games. And so it's more general
cues.zh: DeepMind早期的成就之一，是做出了一个能玩几十种不同Atari游戏的程序，单个程序就能学会所有这些不同的游戏。所以它更通用

cues.en: because it's able to act across a wider variety of domains.
cues.zh: 因为它能够跨越更广泛的领域来行动。

cues.en: The most general intelligence that we're aware of right now is human beings.
cues.zh: 我们目前所知的最通用的智能是人类。

cues.en: Human beings are very general. We're able to operate across a very wide range of domains
cues.zh: 人类非常通用。我们能够在非常广泛的领域中运作

cues.en: including, and this is important, we're able to learn domains which
cues.zh: 包括——这一点很重要——我们能够学习那些

cues.en: evolution did not and could not prepare us for.
cues.zh: 进化没有也无法为我们准备好应对的领域。

cues.en: We can, for example, drive a car and evolution did not prepare us for that. We invented cars. They're very recent.
cues.zh: 比如，我们能开车，而进化并没有为此准备我们。汽车是我们发明的，出现得非常晚。

cues.en: We can, you know, invent rockets and go to the moon, and then we can operate on the moon, which is a completely different environment. And this is kind of the power of general intelligence. Really, the power of general intelligence is we can build a car. We can build a rocket. We can put the car on the rocket, take the car to the moon, drive the car on the moon.
cues.zh: 我们能发明火箭、登上月球，然后在月球上作业，那是一个完全不同的环境。这就是通用智能的力量。真正说来，通用智能的力量在于我们能造车，能造火箭，能把车放上火箭，把车带到月球，在月球上开车。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: there's nothing else that can do that yet,
cues.zh: 目前还没有其他东西能做到这一点，

cues.en: but sooner or later.
cues.zh: 但迟早会有的。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: So so this is what I'm talking about. I'm talking about
cues.zh: 所以这就是我在说的。我说的是

cues.en: what you might call true AI, real AI, the sci fi stuff.
cues.zh: 你们可能称之为真正的AI、真正的智能，那种科幻里的东西。

cues.en: An agent which has goals in the real world and is able to intelligently choose actions in the real world to achieve those goals. Now that sounds...
cues.zh: 一个在现实世界中有目标的智能体，能够智能地在现实世界中选择行动来实现那些目标。这听起来……

cues.en: I've said I've said what's the biggest problem? This doesn't sound like a problem. Right?
cues.zh: 我之前问过：最大的问题是什么？这听起来根本不像个问题，对吧？

cues.en: On the surface of it, this sounds like a solution.
cues.zh: 表面上看，这反而像个解决方案。

cues.en: You just tell the thing you know,
cues.zh: 你只要告诉它，比如，

cues.en: cure cancer or maximize the profits of my company or whatever and it takes whatever actions are necessary in the real world to achieve that goal, but it is a problem.
cues.zh: 治愈癌症，或者帮我的公司实现利润最大化之类的，它就会在现实世界中采取一切必要行动来实现目标，但这确实是个问题。

cues.en: So the big problem is this should be auto playing and it isn't.
cues.zh: 那么核心问题是——等等，这视频本来应该自动播放的，结果没有。

cues.en: The big problem is it's difficult to
cues.zh: 核心问题在于，我们很难

cues.en: choose good goals.
cues.zh: 设定出好的目标。

cues.en: So this this is an AI made by OpenAI. It's playing a game called Coast Runners, which is actually a racing game. They trained it on the score, which you probably can't see down here. It's currently a thousand.
cues.zh: 这是 OpenAI 做的一个 AI。它正在玩一款叫 Coast Runners 的游戏，其实是个赛艇竞速游戏。他们拿得分来训练它，下面你们可能看不清，现在是一千分。

cues.en: What the system learned is that if it goes around in a circle here and crashes into everything and catches fire, these little turbo pickups, they respawn at just the right rate that if it just flings itself around in a circle, it can pick up the turbo and that gives you a few points every time you do that and it turns out that this is a much better way of getting points than actually
cues.zh: 系统学到的是，如果它就在这里转圈，到处乱撞甚至起火，那些小小的加速道具刷新的频率刚好能让它只要转圈就能吃到，每次吃到都会给点分，事实证明，这种得分方式远胜于真正去

cues.en: racing
cues.zh: 竞速

cues.en: around the track.
cues.zh: 跑完赛道。

cues.en: And the important point here is
cues.zh: 这里的关键点在于，

cues.en: that this is not unusual. This is not OpenAI doing anything unusually stupid. This is kind of the default.
cues.zh: 这种情况并不罕见。并不是 OpenAI 做了什么格外愚蠢的事，这其实算是一种常态。

cues.en: Picking objectives objectives is surprisingly hard and you will find that
cues.zh: 设定目标出奇地难，而且你会发现，

cues.en: the strategy or the behavior that maximizes your objective is probably not the thing you thought it was. It's probably not what you were aiming for. There's loads of examples. Actually, Victoria has a great list on her blog deep safety. There's like 30 of them. Different things going wrong. There was one they had...
cues.zh: 能把目标最大化的策略或行为，往往跟你预想的完全不同，很可能根本不是你想要的结果。这种例子数不胜数。实际上 Victoria 在她的博客 deep safety 上整理了一份很棒的清单，大概列了 30 个各种翻车的案例。比如有一次他们……

cues.en: They were trying to teach... They were trying to evolve systems that would run quickly, so they they trained them on the... I'm gonna pause this because it's distracting as hell.
cues.zh: 他们试图训练……他们试图演化出能快速奔跑的系统，所以他们训练它们……我得先暂停一下，因为这太让人分心了。

cues.en: Where's my mouse? You're mesmerizing. Yeah.
cues.zh: 我的鼠标在哪？你太让人着迷了。好。

cues.en: Pause. Pause, please.
cues.zh: 暂停。请暂停一下。

cues.en: They were training like agents that were supposed to run. So they simulated them for a particular period of time and measured how far their center of mass moved, which seems perfectly sensible. What they found was that they developed a bunch of these creatures which were extremely tall and thin with a big mass on the end that then fell over because they weren't simulating them for long enough that you could go the fastest just by falling over rather than actually running. That moved your center of mass the furthest.
cues.zh: 他们当时在训练理应去奔跑的智能体。他们让智能体模拟运行了一段时间，并测量其质心移动了多远，这看起来完全合情合理。结果他们发现，系统演化出了一堆又高又细、顶端很沉的生物，然后直接倒了下去；因为模拟时间不够长，直接倒下反而比真正奔跑能更快移动质心，那样能让质心移动得最远。

cues.en: There's a lot of these. There was a Tetris bot which
cues.zh: 这类例子还有很多。曾经有个 Tetris 机器人，它

cues.en: would
cues.zh: 会

cues.en: play reasonably well and then just when it was about to lose, would pause the game and sit there indefinitely because it lost points for losing but didn't lose any points for just sitting on the pause screen indefinitely.
cues.zh: 玩得还算不错，但就在快要输掉的时候，它会暂停游戏并一直停在那里，因为输了会扣分，但一直停在暂停画面上却不会扣分。

cues.en: This is this is like the default of how these systems behave. I have no memory what my next slide is. Oh, yeah. Right. So we have problems specifying even simple goals in simple environments like Atari games or basic
cues.zh: 这就是这类系统典型的行为方式。我完全不记得下一张幻灯片是什么了。噢，对，没错。所以即使在像 Atari 游戏这样的简单环境，或者基础的

cues.en: evolutionary algorithms, things like that. When it comes to the real world, things get way more complicated. This is a quote from Stuart Russell, who sort of wrote the book on AI. When a system is optimizing a function of n variables where the objective depends on a subset of size k, which is less than n, it will often set the remaining unconstrained variables to extreme values.
cues.zh: 演化算法这类场景中，我们甚至都很难明确定义简单的目标。而一旦进入现实世界，情况会复杂得多。这是 Stuart Russell 的一句话，他算是写过 AI 经典教材的权威：“当一个系统在优化包含 n 个变量的函数，而目标仅取决于大小为 k（k < n）的子集时，它往往会将剩余不受约束的变量推向极端值。”

cues.en: If one of those unconstrained variables is something that we care about, the solution found may be highly undesirable. In the real world, we have a very large number of variables. And so we were talking about
cues.zh: 如果这些无约束变量中有一个是我们关心的，找到的解可能非常不可取。在现实世界中，我们有非常多的变量。所以我们刚才在讨论

cues.en: we're talking about very large values for n here. So let's say you've got your robot
cues.zh: 我们在这里讨论的是非常大的n值。假设你有一个机器人

cues.en: and you've given it a goal which you think is very simple. You want it to get you a cup of tea.
cues.zh: 你给它设定了一个你认为非常简单的目标。你想让它给你拿一杯茶。

cues.en: So you've managed to specify what a cup of tea is and that you want one to be on the desk in front of you.
cues.zh: 你已经成功定义了什么是“一杯茶”，并且你希望一杯茶放在你面前的桌子上。

cues.en: So far so good.
cues.zh: 到目前为止一切顺利。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: suppose there is a there's a price of something bars on a narrow stand sort of in front of where the kitchen is. So the robot immediately
cues.zh: 假设厨房前面有个窄架子上放着什么贵重物品。于是机器人立刻

cues.en: plows into the bars and destroys it on its way to make you a cup of tea because you only gave it one variable to keep track of in the goal, which is the tea. It doesn't care about the vase. You never told it to care about the vase. It destroys the vase. This is a problem.
cues.zh: 冲过去，在给你拿茶的路上把它撞毁，因为你只让它在目标中关注一个变量，也就是茶。它不在乎花瓶。你从没告诉它要在乎花瓶。它把花瓶毁了。这就是问题所在。

cues.en: So okay. Now you can,
cues.zh: 好吧。现在你可以，

cues.en: you know, shut it down, modify it, and say,
cues.zh: 你知道，把它关掉，改一改，然后说，

cues.en: okay. Get me a cup of tea, but also don't knock over the vase.

cues.en: But then there will be a third thing. There is always another thing because
cues.zh: 但然后还会有第三件事。总会有另一件事，因为

cues.en: when when you're making decisions in the real world, you're always making trade offs. You're always taking various things that you value and deciding how much of one you're willing to trade for how much of another. You know, I could do this quicker, but it increases the risk of me making a mistake.
cues.zh: 当你在现实世界中做决定时，你总是在做权衡。你总是在拿你重视的各种东西，决定你愿意用多少这个去换多少那个。你知道，我可以做得更快，但这会增加我犯错的几率。

cues.en: Or I could do this cheaper, but it won't be as reliable. I could do this faster, but it'll be more expensive. That you're always trading these things off against one another. And so
cues.zh: 我也可以做得更便宜，但可靠性会差一些。我也可以做得更快，但成本会更高。你总是在这些因素之间做权衡。所以

cues.en: an agent like this, which only cares about a limited subset of the variables in the system,
cues.zh: 像这样的智能体，只关心系统中有限的一部分变量，

cues.en: will be willing to trade off arbitrarily large amounts of any of the variables that aren't part of its goal for arbitrarily tiny increases in any of things which are in its goal. So it will happily...
cues.zh: 就会愿意牺牲任意大量的、不属于它目标的变量，来换取它目标中任意微小的提升。所以它会毫不犹豫地……

cues.en: And let's say now, for example, now it values the vase,
cues.zh: 假设现在，举个例子，它现在看重这个花瓶，

cues.en: and those are the only things that it values. It might reason something like,
cues.zh: 而这是它唯一看重的东西。它可能会这样推理，

cues.en: okay, there... There's a human in the environment. Environment. The The human human moves moves around. Around. The human may accidentally knock over the vase
cues.zh: 好吧，那里……环境里有个 人。环境。那个 人 人 在 四处 走动。走动。人可能会不小心碰倒花瓶

cues.en: and I care about the vase, so I have to kill the human. Right? And this is totally ridiculous,
cues.zh: 而我在意花瓶，所以我必须杀掉那个人。对吧？这完全荒谬，

cues.en: but if you didn't tell it that you value being alive, it doesn't care. And anything that it doesn't value
cues.zh: 但如果你没告诉它你看重活着，它就不在乎。而任何它不看重的

cues.en: is going to be lost. If you manage to come up with... If you have a sufficiently powerful agent and you manage to come up with a really good objective function which covers the top 20 things that humans value,
cues.zh: 都会被牺牲掉。如果你能想出……如果你有一个足够强大的智能体，并且你能想出一个非常好的目标函数，覆盖了人类最看重的 20 件事，

cues.en: the twenty first thing that humans value is probably gone forever
cues.zh: 人类看重的第 21 件事很可能就永远消失了

cues.en: Because
cues.zh: 因为

cues.en: the smarter, the more powerful the agent is, the better it will be at figuring out ways to make these trade offs. To gain a millionth of a percent better at one thing while sacrificing
cues.zh: 智能体越聪明、越强大，它就越擅长找出办法来做这些权衡。在某一件事上提升百万分之一，同时牺牲

cues.en: everything of some other variable.
cues.zh: 另一个变量的全部。

cues.en: So this is a problem. But actually that scenario I gave was unrealistic in
cues.zh: 所以这是个问题。但事实上，我给出的那个场景在

cues.en: many ways. But
cues.zh: 很多方面都不现实。但

cues.en: one important way that it was unrealistic
cues.zh: 它不现实的一个重要方面

cues.en: is that I had I had the system go wrong and then you just turn it off and fix it. But in fact, if you're...
cues.zh: 是我让系统出了错，然后你只要把它关掉再修好。但事实上，如果你……

cues.en: If the thing has a goal of getting you a cup of tea, this is not like a chess AI where you can just turn it off because it has no concept of itself or being turned off.
cues.zh: 如果这东西的目标是给你弄一杯茶，那它就不像国际象棋 AI，你可以直接把它关掉，因为它没有自我概念，也没有被关掉的概念。

cues.en: Its world model contains you, it contains itself, it contains the possibility of being turned off and it's fully aware that if you turn it off because it knocked over the bars, it won't be able to get you any tea, which is the only thing it cares about. So it's not gonna just let you turn it off. It will fight you.
cues.zh: 它的世界模型包含你，包含它自己，包含被关掉的可能性；而且它完全清楚，如果你因为它撞倒了栏杆而关掉它，它就没法给你弄到任何茶，而这是它唯一在乎的事。所以它不会就这么让你把它关掉。它会跟你对抗。

cues.en: Or if it's slightly smarter, it will deceive you so that you believe it's working correctly, so that you don't want to change it until it's in a position where you can't turn it off. And then it will go after its actual objective.
cues.zh: 或者，如果它稍微聪明一点，它会欺骗你，让你相信它运行正常，这样你就不想改它，直到它到了你无法关掉它的地步。然后它就会去追求它真正的目标。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: this is a problem.
cues.zh: 这是个问题。

cues.en: And and the thing is this is this is a convergent instrumental goal, which means it sort of doesn't matter what the goal is. It doesn't matter what your goal is as an agent. If you're destroyed, you can't achieve that goal. So it sort of almost doesn't matter what goal we give it. There is only a very tiny fraction of possible goals that will involve it
cues.zh: 而且，关键在于，这是一个趋同的工具性目标，这意味着目标是什么其实有点无所谓。作为智能体，你的目标是什么也无所谓。如果你被毁灭了，你就无法实现那个目标。所以，我们给它什么目标几乎都无所谓。只有极小一部分可能的目标会涉及它

cues.en: actually
cues.zh: 真正

cues.en: allowing itself to be turned off and modified.
cues.zh: 允许自己被关掉并修改。

cues.en: And that's quite complicated.
cues.zh: 而那相当复杂。

cues.en: There are some other convergent instrumental goals. So we had self preservation, goal preservation. Resource acquisition is the kind of thing we can expect these kinds of systems to do.
cues.zh: 还有其他一些趋同的工具性目标。我们有自我保存、目标保存。资源获取是我们可以预期这类系统会去做的事情。

cues.en: Most plans, you can do them better if you have more resources,
cues.zh: 大多数计划，如果你有更多资源，就能做得更好，

cues.en: whether that's money, computational resources, just free energy matter, whatever.
cues.zh: 无论是金钱、计算资源，还是自由能源物质，诸如此类。

cues.en: The other one is self improvement.
cues.zh: 另一个是自我改进。

cues.en: Whatever you're trying to do, you can probably do it better if you're smarter.
cues.zh: 无论你想做什么，如果你更聪明，大概就能做得更好。

cues.en: And AI systems potentially have the capacity to improve themselves either just by acquiring more hardware to run on or changing, you know, improving their
cues.zh: 而AI系统有可能具备自我改进的能力，要么通过获取更多硬件来运行，要么改变、改进它们的

cues.en: software to run faster or better or so on. So there's a whole bunch of behaviors
cues.zh: 软件以运行得更快或更好等等。所以有一大堆行为

cues.en: which
cues.zh: 是

cues.en: intelligent systems, intelligent agents, generally intelligent agents,
cues.zh: 智能系统、智能体、通用智能体，

cues.en: we would expect them to do by default.
cues.zh: 我们预期它们默认就会去做的。

cues.en: And that's really
cues.zh: 而这正是

cues.en: my core point. Artificial general intelligence is dangerous by default.
cues.zh: 我的核心观点。通用人工智能默认就是危险的。

cues.en: It's much much easier
cues.zh: 要构建这类智能体——它们试图做荒谬的事情、欺骗你、试图蒙骗你，或者在你试图关掉或修改它们时与你对抗——

cues.en: to build these kinds of agents which try to do ridiculous things and trick you and try to deceive you or will fight you when you try to turn them off or modify them
cues.zh: 在去做某些你不想要的荒谬事情的过程中，

cues.en: on the way to doing some ridiculous thing which you don't want.
cues.zh: 要容易得多。

cues.en: Much easier to build that kind of agent than it is to build something which actually reliably does what you want it to do.
cues.zh: 构建那种智能体，比构建真正能可靠地做你想让它做的事的东西，要容易得多。

cues.en: And that's why we have a problem because we have
cues.zh: 这就是为什么我们面临问题，因为我们只有

cues.en: forty five to a hundred and twenty years to figure out how to do it safely,
cues.zh: 四十五到一百二十年的时间来弄清楚如何安全地做到这一点，

cues.en: which is a much harder problem.
cues.zh: 而这是一个难得得多的问题。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: And

cues.en: we may only get one shot. It's entirely possible that the first true artificial general intelligence
cues.zh: 我们可能只有一次机会。很可能第一个真正的通用人工智能

cues.en: will
cues.zh: 会

cues.en: manage to successfully achieve whatever its stupid goal is.
cues.zh: 成功实现它那个愚蠢的目标。

cues.zh: 我们还有办法。安全的通用人工智能完全有可能实现。

cues.zh: 只是这是个非常困难的
